description: Collection of assets that work together as a system to collect, treat, store, and deliver water to users

Physical location where specific functions are performed in the production, treatment, and delivery of water; the use of water facilities is optional and can be used to organize or locate the assets contained in large and complex treatment and distribution systems
Location where a supply of water, such as a lake, river, spring, or groundwater aquifer, is abstracted for use in a distribution system
Mechanical or electromechanical device that increases the hydraulic head (pressure) of a fluid flowing through it
Structure or container used to hold water or other fluids
Device that supplies electrical power for use by electrical equipment, such as a generator, solar power system, wind turbine, or connection to a power grid
Equipment or process that improves the physical, chemical, biological, or aesthetic quality of water
Device for measuring the Flow rate of water through a pipe
Any electrical or electronic device
Mechanical device designed to close off or regulate the flow of water
Device that provides the equipment needed to attach a fire hose to a water distribution network for use in extinguishing fires
Section of a piped network that joins two or more pipes or conduits
Location or access point in a water distribution network that allows for a water sample to be collected for testing
Device that measures a physical condition or parameter of interest
Device that conducts periodic or continuous measurements of a water quality parameter
Anything that is constructed or built with a fixed location on the ground
Location or facility where users can access water
Any other type of vertical asset not defined elsewhere in this standard
Conduit that carries water or other fluids from one location to another
Artificial open channel or waterway constructed for transporting water, connecting two or more bodies of water, or serving as a waterway
Impounded body of water or controlled lake in which water can be collected and stored
Large stream of water that serves as the natural drainage
Geologic formation that is saturated and sufficiently permeable to transmit useful quantities of water to wells and springs
Concentrated discharge of groundwater appearing at the ground surface
Banks or immediate border of a stream or river
Shallow pond or depression used to infiltrate stormwater or runoff through permeable soils into a groundwater aquifer
Land area characterized by woody vegetation greater than about 5 meters in height

Area that is inundated or saturated by surface water or groundwater at a frequency and duration sufficient to support a vegetation adapted for life in saturated soil conditions; includes swamps, marshes, and bogs
Area from which water drains and contributes to a particular stream or river
